text.text: A profile of a protein family: it searches with one protein, builds a profile from the hits, and searches again with that profile, three rounds in all.

Is the closest same-family domain in the relative you will search at least 40% identical, for most of your proteins? If yes, Fmax here is 40–60% 0.217 (n = 563), 60–100% 0.264 (n = 1,289). If no, 20–30% 0.327 (n = 93), 30–40% 0.175 (n = 165). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (430 Mya) as the relative searched, setting 3 rounds; subsets with at least 30 true instances.)

Are the features you care about longer than 60 residues? If yes, Fmax here is 61–120 aa 0.210 (n = 963), 121–250 aa 0.333 (n = 504), 251 aa or more 0.427 (n = 277). If no, 16–30 aa 0.029 (n = 271), 31–60 aa 0.066 (n = 420). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (430 Mya) as the relative searched, setting 3 rounds.)
Can you spend about 2.45 core-hours per 1,000 proteins for each relative you search? That is the measured mean per relative; see "Cost per 1,000 queries" below.

Under the Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (430 Mya) as the relative searched, its best setting is 3 rounds (n3): Fmax 0.290 over 2,435 true instances. Searching costs about $0.109 per 1,000 queries (2.45 core-hours), for each relative searched.
Where it is strong and weak

Each line compares this setting with the best setting of any other tool on the same subset of the proteins, so the other tool's setting can change from line to line. Only subsets with at least 30 true instances are compared.
Where it is closest to, or furthest ahead of, the best other tool:
regions 121–250 aa long: Fmax 0.333 (n = 504); best other: phmmer, default options, 0.329.
no same-family domain in the relative: Fmax 0.023 (n = 321); best other: HH-suite (hhsearch), single-protein profiles, 0.032.
Where it is furthest behind the best other tool:
regions 16–30 aa long: Fmax 0.029 (n = 271); best other: kmerseek, wwmj5, k = 11, 0.330.
regions 31–60 aa long: Fmax 0.066 (n = 420); best other: kmerseek, gbmr4, k = 21, 0.232.
Swiss-Prot features, raw calls, zebrafish, setting 3 rounds: best feature type active site, Fmax 0.287 (n = 176); worst short motif, Fmax 0.002 (n = 190).
Can its weak hits be trusted?

When this tool's best hit on a protein is weak, is it right? It was measured on the dark set of four species, each searched against Swiss-Prot without its own clade. Dark proteins have no phmmer, jackhmmer or MMseqs2 hit at E ≤ 1; placed proteins are the rest. A best hit is right when the target shares a Pfam family with the query and the hit covers a Pfam domain of that family on the query. n counts the best hits whose target has any Pfam family. Test half of the proteins only. Grey: fewer than 30 judged hits (how it was measured).
Setting in the dark-set run: jackhmmer, 3 rounds (-N 3), E ≤ 10.
PR 133's looser test counts a shared Pfam family or clan anywhere on the two proteins. By that test, on dark proteins at E 1–10:

Figure 2. Where jackhmmer is ahead and behind: its Fmax on each subset of the proteins, against the best other tool on that subset (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish as the relative; its best setting, 3 rounds). Left out, under 30 true instances: 0–20%.
A profile of a protein family: it searches with one protein, builds a profile from the hits, and searches again with that profile, three rounds in all.
The relative's proteome (Quest for Orthologs reference proteomes, release 2020_04), as a FASTA file.
Domain bit score: higher ranks first. The E-value cutoff was 10.
Each round can pull in proteins from a different family, which then pull in more. How often that happened here: not measured.

Setting n3, searching one relative (mean over the 15 relatives it searched): 2.45 core-hours reserved per 1,000 queries (8 cores for the task's wall time), measured on Sherlock. Peak memory 5.2 GB. That is about $0.109 at $0.044625 per CPU-hour. Building its databases for setting n3: not measured (no task record holds a database build for this tool and setting).
The per-query cost counts the search only. The run recorded cost per tool and setting, summed over all relatives, so the cost for one relative is the mean.
Query: 998 human proteins. Target: the zebrafish proteome.
Tool id hmmer3_jackhmmer. Numbers from seanome/2024-kmerseek-analysis commit 4a4b1171.
